data.title: Sailor Moon Anime Goes Retro With Creditless Cosmos Film Opening
data.author: Daryl Harding
data.description:
The first of the two films is currently in Japanese theaters

The official Sailor Moon YouTube account released an updated version of the “Moonlight Densetsu” in the new animation style and with all the latest characters for the Cosmos anime film. Check it out after the jump!
data.content:
For anime fans over a certain age, the original Sailor Moon anime opening (both the English or Japanese versions) is etched into our hearts and minds. For the release of the first Sailor Moon Cosmos anime film, the official YouTube account released an updated version of the “Moonlight Densetsu (Moonlight Legend)” in the new animation style and with all the latest characters.

 

 

The video not only serves as a homage to the original (and beloved!) 1992 opening but is also the opening title for the first Sailor Moon Cosmos anime film, which is currently playing in theaters across Japan.

 

RELATED: Sailor Moon Cosmos Anime Gets Smol in Latest Character Transformation Video

 

What’s more, the third-week theatrical gift for the first Sailor Moon Cosmos anime film was also announced. Starting June 23, four coasters featuring illustrations drawn by character designer Kazuko Tadano will be given out randomly to those who see the film in Japan.

 

 

Sailor Moon Cosmos is adapting the "final battle" from the original manga series by Naoko Takeuchi, which was previously adapted as the last arc of the original Sailor Moon anime dubbed "Sailor Moon Sailor Stars." Cosmos' first film was released on June 9, while the second part enters theaters on June 30.

 

Cosmos continues from the Sailor Moon Eternal two-part film, released in early 2021 in Japan and worldwide on Netflix on June 3, 2021. Eternal continued the Sailor Moon Crystal TV anime series, which is streaming here on Crunchyroll, who describes the series:

 

Based on Naoko Takeuchi’s legendary manga series, Sailor Moon Crystal retells the story of Sailor Moon as she searches for her fellow Sailor Guardians and the Legendary Silver Crystal to stop the dark forces of Queen Beryl.

 

Source: Comic Natalie

 

---- 

Daryl Harding is a Senior Japan Correspondent for Crunchyroll News. He also runs a YouTube channel about Japan stuff called TheDoctorDazza, tweets at @DoctorDazza, and posts photos of his travels on Instagram.

data.title: Baten Kaitos 1 and 2 HD Remaster Takes Flight in September
data.author: George Yang
data.description:
Both Origins and Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean are newly remastered

Baten Kaitos 1 and 2 Remastered will finally release on the Nintendo Switch on September 14. Read on for more!
data.content:
Bandai Namco announced that Baten Kaitos I & II HD Remaster will launch for Nintendo Switch on September 14. The package includes both games in the series originally released on the Nintendo GameCube. Check out the release date trailer below:

 

 

Baten Kaitos: Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean follows the story of Kalas who goes on a journey to avenge his brother and grandfather's deaths. He meets a young woman named Xelha and band together to defeat the Alfard Empire. Baten Kaitos Origins (known as Baten Kaitos II in Japan) is a prequel set 20 years before the events of Eternal Wings and the Lost Ocean. It follows a spiriter named Sagi who works for the Alfard Empire as part of an elite unit called the Dark Service. After being framed, Sagi sets out on a journey to clear his name and to reveal the empire's deepest secrets.

 

RELATED: Waboku & A-1 Pictures' BATEN KAITOS Project Releases NIGHT HEAD 2041 ED Theme MV

 

Those who purchase the game early on during its release period will receive a digital artbook that includes art from the original game design documents and visuals.

 

Source: Press Release

 

 

 

George Yang is a freelance writer specializing in video games and pop culture. He has written for sites like IGN, GameSpot, Kotaku, The Verge, NPR, and Complex. You can follow him on Twitter @yinyangfooey.

data.title: SPY x FAMILY CODE: White Anime Film Releases New Teaser Visual

data.description:
An "exciting family trip" premieres this December!

A treasure chest, a locomotive, lipstick and more make up the packed contents of SPY x FAMILY CODE: White's latest visual, clueing us into the anime film's itinerary ahead of a December premiere in Japan. Hit the jump for the full picture!
data.content:
SPY x FAMILY has just the ticket for fans eagerly waiting for the next leg of the Forger family's adventures, today unveiling a teaser visual jam-packed with clues about upcoming anime film SPY x FAMILY CODE: White, which is scheduled to premiere in Japan on December 22. Teaser Visual

data.title: Japan Box Office: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse Makes 2nd Place Debut
data.author: Mikikazu Komatsu
data.description:
"Rohan at the Louvre" live-action film also surpasses one billion yen

The CG animation superhero film Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse opened in 354 theaters in Japan on June 16, two weeks after its US release, then earned 396 million yen (2.8 million USD) on 249,000 admissions in its first three days, making its second place debut in the weekend box office ranking. Hit the jump for more details!
data.content:
The CG animation superhero film Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse, the sequel to the 2018 film Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, opened in 354 theaters in Japan on June 16, two weeks after its US release, earning 396 million yen (2.8 million USD) on 249,000 admissions in its first three days and making its second place debut in the weekend box office ranking. The first-weekend gross was a huge 182 percent of that of the first film, which made 900 million yen (6.35 million USD) from its total theatrical run in Japan.

 

The 140-minute film has also been well-received by Japanese audience, ranking No.1 in Filmarks' first-day satisfaction ranking with an average rating of 4.4/5.0 based on 6,640 reviews.

 

RELATED: LiSA Releases Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse Japanese Theme Song Lyric Video

 

While disappearing from the top 10 in its fourth weekend, the cumulative total box office gross of the live-action feature film adaptation of Hirohiko Araki's Rohan at the Louvre (Rohan au Louvre) manga has finally surpassed one billion yen (7.03 million USD) on 720,000 admissions in 24 days since its release.

 

Rohan at the Louvre is one of the episodes in Thus Spoke Kishibe Rohan, a spin-off to Araki's long-running JoJo's Bizarre Adventure series, with the protagonist Rohan Kishibe is one of the main characters in JoJo's fourth installment, Diamond is Unbreakable. Its live-action TV drama series starring Issey Takahashi as Rohan aired for eight episodes on NHK General TV between 2020 and 2022. This is the first time that a film version of a live-action drama series broadcast on NHK has grossed over one billion yen at the Japanese box office. 

 

As previously reported, the cumulative total box office of the male idol-themed multimedia franchise IDOLiSH7's first concert film IDOLiSH 7 LIVE 4bit BEYOND THE PERiOD has also reached a milestone of one billion yen (7.03 million USD) in five weeks since its release. The 93-minute film was released in Japan on May 20 and still ranked ninth, the same position from the previous weekend, in its fifth weekend.

 

RELATED: IDOLiSH7 Concert Film Finally Reaches One Billion Yen Mark in Japan

 

The Detective Conan anime franchise's 26th feature film, Detective Conan: Black Iron Submarine, dropped to 10th in its 10th weekend, four places down from the previous weekend.

 

Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King, the feature film edition of the Black Clover anime franchise based on Yuuki Tabata's action fantasy manga of the same name, was also released in 101 theaters across Japan on June 16. The 113-minute film failed to make its top 10 debut at the weekend box office and ranked fifth in Filmarks' first-day satisfaction ranking with an average rating of 3.63/5.0 based on 226 reviews.

 

RELATED: See How Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King Anime Film Opens

data.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Places 25th Anniversary Card Down at GU in Clothing Collab Position
data.author: Daryl Harding
data.description:
Hoodies, sweatshirts and more don the iconic symbols

Next year will mark 25 years since the Yu-Gi-Oh! trading card game launched in Japan and to mark the momentous occasion, the card game is teaming up with Japanese clothing shop GU to release some commemorative apparel.
data.content:
Next year will mark 25 years since the Yu-Gi-Oh! trading card game launched in Japan and to mark the momentous occasion, the card game is teaming up with Japanese clothing shop GU to release some commemorative apparel. The range includes hoodies, sweatshirts, socks and even boxer shorts to dress in that card game drip.

 

The hoodies, which are 2,990 yen (US$21) each:

 

 

The sweatshirts, which are 1,990 yen (US$14) each:

 

 

The boxer shorts, which are 590 yen (US$4) each:

 

 

 

The socks which are 390 yen (US$2.75) each:

 

 

 

 

 

RELATED: Send Your Foes to the Shadow Realm with Yu-Gi-Oh! Fashion

 

The full line-up will be released in GU stores across Japan from mid-September, bringing everyone into the world of card games! You can also watch the original Yu-Gi-Oh! anime series right here on Crunchyroll, who describes the series: 

 

Meet Yugi and his best buds Joey, Tristan and Téa. They share a love for the newest game that’s sweeping the nation: Duel Monsters!

 

Legend has it 5000 years ago, ancient Egyptian Pharaohs used to play a magical game very similar to Duel Monsters. This ancient game involved magical ceremonies, which were used to foresee the future and ultimately decide one’s destiny. They called it the Shadow Games. Since the game used so many magical spells and ferocious creatures, it wasn’t long before the game got out of hand and threatened to destroy the world.

data.title: Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead TV Anime Reveals English Dub Cast
data.author: Liam Dempsey
data.description:
New trailer showcases Zeno Robinson as the voice of Akira

Horror-comedy anime Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead is already getting a gang together for English dub fans to take on the apocalypse, today revealing an official trailer and main cast members. A release date was also announced, so hit the jump for all the details!
data.content:
English dub fans can already tick off one title from the fast-approaching summer 2023 anime season, as horror-comedy anime Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead got ahead of the pack today by revealing four main cast members and an official trailer.

 

Here's who'll be living it up in the apocalypse when the dub arrives on Netflix and Hulu from August 6:

 

  • Akira voiced by Zeno Robinson (Vanitas in The Case Study of Vanitas)
  • Shizuka voiced by Abby Trott (Nezuko in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba)
  • Kencho voiced by Xander Mobus (Todo in JUJUTSU KAISEN)
  • Beatrix voiced by Laura Post (Cynthia in Great Pretender)

 

English Dub Trailer

 

RELATED: Zom 100: Bucket List of the Dead Anime Adds Two Cast Members in English-Subbed Trailer

 

Based on the manga by Haro Aso and Kotaro Takata, Kazuki Kawagoe is directing the series at studio BUG FILMS, with series composition by Hiroshi Seko (JUJUTSU KAISEN), character designs by Kii Tanaka (So I'm a Spider, So What?) and music by Makoto Miyazaki (One Punch Man). The anime adaptation is scheduled to begin airing on July 9, with simultaneous international streaming from Netflix and Hulu.

 

VIZ Media, which publishes the manga's official English version, describes the series:

 

With three years under his belt at the company from hell, Akira Tendo is mentally and physically spent.

 

All at the ripe old age of twenty-four. Even his crush from Accounting, Saori, wants nothing to do with him.

 

Then, just when life is beginning to look like one big disappointment, it happens.

 

The zombie apocalypse descends on Japan!

 

Surrounded by hordes of hungry zombies, Akira comes to a realization that will forever change his life...

 

“Wait, does this mean I never have to go to work again?”

 

Confess to... party like it’s... travel Japan coast to...

 

Now, with his nightmare job no longer, Akira’s got his mojo back. Let the bucket listing begin!!

 

Source: VIZ Media on Twitter

data.title: Pokémon Worlds in Japan Evolves to Include Weeklong PokéEvents
data.author: Daryl Harding
data.description:
Pikachu will be taking over Yokohama starting August 8

This year, the Pokémon World Championships are returning to Japan for the first time in a while and with it comes an array of PokéFun events. Catch all the details after the jump!
data.content:
Every August, Pokémon takes over the port town of Yokohama just south of Tokyo with events such as the Pikachu Outbreak march and other summer fun — though that stopped due to the pandemic. This year, the Pokémon World Championships are returning to Japan for the first time in a while, putting the yearly plans up in the air until now.

 

Not only will the Pikachu Outbreak return to Yokohama this year with one of the biggest parades ever on the Monday, but alongside the Pokémon World Championships will be the Pokémon Center Worlds with some exclusive merchandise, three Pokémon Fantastic Live Shows — We Move!!, Imagination! Into the Next!! and Pikachu Gathering!! — the Pokémon Trainer Cruise, and the Pokémon Matsuri Park, with stalls inspired by a normal matsuri with a Pokémon theme.

 

RELATED: Pokémon Horizons TV Anime Casts Japanese Voices for Nemona, Brassius

 

Pokémon decorations will also be all over Yokohama under the Pokégenic banner. Here is a preview of them:

 

 

Tickets for all the events, including the Pokémon Center Worlds but excluding the cruise and Pikachu Gathering!!! show, are only available through a lottery system with applications available until July 3. All events will be held in Yokohama’s Minatomirai area from August 8 to 14.


Source: Pokémon official website

 

---- 

Daryl Harding is a Senior Japan Correspondent for Crunchyroll News. He also runs a YouTube channel about Japan stuff called TheDoctorDazza, tweets at @DoctorDazza, and posts photos of his travels on Instagram.

data.title: Maaya Sakamoto Releases Statement on Her Health Condition After Concert Postponement
data.author: Mikikazu Komatsu
data.description:
Sakamoto has been diagnosed with vocal cord inflammation

After the postponement of her concert scheduled for June 18 in Osaka, voice actress/singer Maaya Sakamoto posted a statement on Flying Dog's official Twitter account explaining her current health condition. Hit the jump for more details.
data.content:
After the postponement of her concert scheduled for June 18 in Osaka, voice actress/singer Maaya Sakamoto posted a statement on Flying Dog's official Twitter account explaining her current health condition.

 

RELATED: Maaya Sakamoto Releases New Music Video "Naimononedari" from Her 11th Album 

 

Sakamoto started her solo concert tour, "Sakamoto Maaya LIVE TOUR 2023 'Kioku no Toshokan,'" in Saitama on June 2. After performing in Aichi on June 4 and in Osaka on June 17, she canceled the second day of her scheduled show in Osaka due to her throat condition.

 

Sakamoto's statement follows:

 

I'm sorry to have worried you. Thank you to everyone who has sent me warm messages. Upon my return to Tokyo, my family doctor again diagnosed me with vocal cord inflammation. My voice is hoarse, but my body is in very good health, thankfully. Now I am trying to recover, imagining that I will be able to enjoy the next weekend with my audience. I had been taking extra care of myself because I was in the middle of a tour, but I am very sorry for the inconvenience to those who have tickets for the second day of Osaka. If I am able to hold this concert on a different day, I hope to make up for this by singing with all my heart and soul.

 

【#坂本真綾】

坂本真綾より皆様へ pic.twitter.com/BRw74xi2rr

— フライングドッグ (@FlyingDogInc) June 19, 2023

 

Her next shows in the current tour are scheduled for June 24 and 25 at Tokyo Garden Theater in Tokyo, and at the time of reporting they will be held as scheduled. No decision has been made yet regarding a replacement for the postponed second day of the Osaka show.

 

Maaya Sakamoto artist photo:

 

Source: Flying Dog official Twitter

data.title: Mugen Souls Z RPG Heads to Nintendo Switch in the West
data.author: Joseph Luster
data.description:
Release planned from eastasiasoft in North America, Europe and Hong Kong

Originally released for PlayStation 3 in Japan back in 2013 before making its way to the rest of the world in 2014, Mugen Souls RPG sequel Mugen Souls Z now has a Nintendo Switch port planned. Read on for more.
data.content:
Originally released for PlayStation 3 in Japan back in 2013 before making its way to the rest of the world in 2014—followed by a PC release in 2016—Mugen Souls RPG sequel Mugen Souls Z now has a Nintendo Switch port planned. A digital release is on the way to North America, Europe and Hong Kong via eastasiasoft, with pre-orders to open through Play-Asia for the physical version on June 22.

 

RELATED: Disgaea 7: Vows of the Virtueless Game Reveals Western Release Dates

 

Check out the announcement trailer and opening movie below.

 

 

 

Physical release:

 

 

Here's how the PC version is described:

 

Join the super-powerful undisputed goddess, Chou-Chou, as she continues her quest to conquer the twelve Zodiac worlds and make everyone and everything her peon.

 

Created by Compile Heart, the developers of Fairy Fencer F and the Agarest and HyperDimension Neptunia series , Mugen Souls Z features free-roaming world maps and a brilliantly flexible turn-based battle system. With the ability to do billions of hit points worth of damage, a level cap of 9999 and some brilliant anime-style artwork, Mugen Souls Z is a game that will satisfy even the most hardcore JRPG player.

 

Twelve worlds corresponding to the signs of the zodiac were created long ago by the ultimate gods and now a certain “something” capable of destroying each of the worlds is preparing to awaken from a long sleep.

 

Chou-Chou and the gang return in this brand-new S-RPG sequel with a new story and even cuter, super-powerful, godly action and adventure! But this time, after her curiosity gets the better of her, Lady Chou-Chou must rely on the abilities of an all-new ultimate goddess, Syrma, as she tries to stop this ancient threat to her world that has recently awakened.

 

‘Chouchers’ must teach this newbie how to become all-powerful, before dealing with a colourful new cast of frenemies, as well as a host of favourites from the first game in the series.

 

Can Syrma work together with Chou-Chou and her motley crew of peons and shampurus to save the twelve worlds from the unknown and ancient “something” that threatens to consume everything in the universe? Join them for 9,999 levels of power levelling, brutal battles and awesome antics to find out!

 

Source: Gematsu

 

 

-------

Joseph Luster is the Games and Web editor at Otaku USA Magazine. You can read his comics at subhumanzoids. Follow him on Twitter @Moldilox.

data.title: Italian Rock Band Måneskin Releases Official BEASTARS Music Video for "TIMEZONE" Song
data.author: Liam Dempsey
data.description:
Like Legoshi and Haru, it's quite the love affair…

Lyrics like "Only thing that keeps us apart is seven thousand miles, running like a mad dog" punctuate the relationship between Legoshi and Haru in a brand-new official music video for "TIMEZONE" by Måneskin, featuring scenes from the BEASTARS manga and a special visual. Hit the jump to check it out!
data.content:
Disclaimer: Crunchyroll is an independently operated joint venture between U.S.-based Sony Pictures Entertainment and Japan’s Aniplex.

 

The only thing keeping apart Paru Itagaki's BEASTARS manga and Italian rock band Måneskin really is just a different timezone, as the odd pair's relationship went to another level today with the release of a Legoshi and Haru-themed music video for "TIMEZONE", featuring scenes from the acclaimed series and a Japanese translation of the lyrics.

 

 

We’re so grateful for this kooool gift from Japan ???? Our song TIMEZONE has now a #BEASTARS visual!! ???????????? Watch here: https://t.co/KxsR4276CC pic.twitter.com/yLgldYUrOA

— MåneskinOfficial (@thisismaneskin) June 19, 2023

 

RELATED: BEASTARS Mangaka Paru Itagaki Meets and Illustrates Italian Rock Band Måneskin

 

Itagaki met and illustrated Måneskin when they were in Japan on tour in September 2022, and went on to publicly praise the group's newest album "RUSH", which includes the "TIMEZONE" track, after its release earlier this year. Their initial meeting reportedly came about due to lead singer Damiano David being a fan of the series.

 

Måneskin begins their Rush! World Tour in September, which currently includes three shows in Tokyo — two of which are already sold out — and one in Kobe in early December.

 

Source: Måneskin on Twitter

data.title: Tokyo Revengers Action-RPG Revealed for Consoles, Mobile and PC
data.author: Joseph Luster
data.description:
Free-to-play game is in the works for a winter release in Japan

On top of the second live-action film on June 30 and the upcoming anime adaptation of the Tenjiku Arc this October, Ken Wakui's Tokyo Revengers manga officially has a game in the works. Read on for more.
data.content:
On top of the second live-action film on June 30 and the upcoming anime adaptation of the Tenjiku Arc this October, Ken Wakui's Tokyo Revengers manga officially has a game in the works. Victor Entertainment announced a new 3D action-RPG for the series, with the Tokyo Revengers game coming in free-to-play form to PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, iOS, Android and PC (DMM GAMES) in Japan this winter.

 

RELATED: Tokyo Revengers TV Anime Teases Tenjiku Arc in New Trailer

 

The Tokyo Revengers action-RPG will have players jumping right into the story of the series in the heart of Shibuya, with the main cast returning in their respective roles. Stay tuned for more information, and check out the brief teaser video below for the first look.

 

 

The first season of the TV anime adaptation of Tokyo Revengers streamed on Crunchyroll as it aired from April to September 2021. The second season, dubbed Tokyo Revengers Christmas Showdown Arc, started streaming worldwide on Disney+ services in January. Crunchyroll describes the series as such:

 

Takemichi Hanagaki is a freelancer that's reached the absolute pits of despair in his life. He finds out that the only girlfriend he ever had in his life that he dated in middle school, Hinata Tachibana, had been killed by the ruthless Tokyo Manji Gang. The day after hearing about her death, he's standing on the station platform and ends up being pushed over onto the tracks by a herd of people. He closes his eyes thinking he's about to die, but when he opens his eyes back up, he somehow had gone back in time 12 years. Now that he's back living the best days of his life, Takemichi decides to get revenge on his life by saving his girlfriend and changing himself that he'd been running away from.

 

Source: Press Release, Gematsu

 

 

-------

Joseph Luster is the Games and Web editor at Otaku USA Magazine. You can read his comics at subhumanzoids. Follow him on Twitter @Moldilox.

data.title: KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World Hits Production Delay
data.author: Paul Chapman
data.description:
Episode 11 of TV anime adaptation will air on June 28 due to “various circumstances”

Citing "various circumstances", the production committee for KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World has announced that Episode 11 of the fantasy manga to TV anime adaptation will be delayed for one week. Read on for more.
data.content:
Even divine beings hit a snag now and then, and due to “various circumstances" the KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World TV anime has hit a production delay that will postpone the release of Episode 11 of the series by one week.

 

According to an official Twitter post by the production committee, Episode 10 will rebroadcast in the show's regular time-slot, while Episode 11 will broadcast in Japan on June 28, 2023.

 

TVアニメ『神無き世界のカミサマ活動』第11話につきまして、諸般の事情により放送を取りやめ、第10話を再放送いたします。
なお、6/28(水)より第11話を順次放送予定です。
本作品を楽しみに待って頂いているお客様により良い作品をお届けできればと思っております。

カミカツ製作委員会 pic.twitter.com/mcOaoHdSpx

— TVアニメ『神無き世界のカミサマ活動』公式放送中 (@kamikatsu_anime) June 19, 2023

 

RELATED: KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World TV Anime to Take One-Week Break

 

Based on the original manga written by Aoi Akashiro and illustrated by Sonsho Hangetsuban, KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World is directed by Yuki Inaba and features animation production by Studio Palette. Crunchyroll currently streams the series, and describes the story as follows:

 

As heir to a cult leader, Yukito centers his life around the mysterious goddess Mitama. But everything changes after he’s killed during a ritual gone wrong. To his surprise, Yukito is reborn into a world with no concept of god! And in this world, life and death are decided by the Imperial State. As Yukito fights to protect his new village, someone from his past life lends a helping hand.

 

Source: KamiKatsu: Working for God in a Godless World on Twitter

 

 

---

Paul Chapman is the host of The Greatest Movie EVER! Podcast and GME! Anime Fun Time.

data.title: Golden Kamuy Season 4 Anime Adds Satoshi Mikami as Abashiri Convict Michael Ostrog
data.author: Joseph Luster
data.description:
The historical action-comedy series is streaming on Crunchyroll

As the adventure continues in the Golden Kamuy anime, a new season 4 cast addition is upon us. Check out the latest after the jump!
data.content:
As the adventure continues in the Golden Kamuy anime, a new season 4 cast addition is upon us. The latest has the adaptation of Satoru Noda's manga introducing Satoshi Mikami (Olcott in Mobile Suit Gundam: The Witch from Mercury) as Abashiri convict Michael Ostrog.

 

RELATED: Golden Kamuy Season 4 Anime Casts Kosuke Toriumi as Takubo Ishikawa

 

Michael Ostrog's anime design:

 

 

Satoshi Mikami:

 

 

Based on the manga by Satoru Noda, Shizutaka Sugahara (Grimms Notes the Animation) is taking over as the chief director of Golden Kamuy at studio Brain's Base from Hitoshi Nanba at Geno Studio. Noboru Takagi continues to write the series composition, while Takumi Yamakawa (animation director on 5 episodes of To Your Eternity) takes over as the character designer.

 

If you're a fan of historical action-comedy anime, check out the first three seasons or all-new episodes of the currently airing fourth every Monday, right here on Crunchyroll!

 

The story takes place in the mighty Northern field of Hokkaido, the time is in the turbulent late Meiji Era. A post war soldier Sugimoto, aka, “Immortal Sugimoto” was in need of large sums of money for a particular purpose….

 

What awaited Sugimoto, who stepped into Hokkaido’s Gold Rush with dreams of making a fortune, was a tattoo map leading to a hidden treasure based on hints inscribed on the bodies of convicts in Abashiri Prison?! data.title: My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1 TV Anime Hunts Treasure in New PV
data.author: Paul Chapman
data.description:
New cast members revealed for upcoming adaptation of isekai fantasy light novel series

A new preview video and two new cast members have been revealed for My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1, an upcoming TV anime based on the series of isekai fantasy light novels about an overworked salaryman who is reborn in a magical world. Read on for more.
data.content:
An energetic new preview video and two new cast members have been revealed for My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1, an upcoming isekai fantasy light novel to TV anime adaptation that begins broadcasting in Japan on TOKYO MX and other stations on July 08, 2023.

 

 

RELATED: My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1 Powers Up on July 8

 

The new cast members include:

 

  • Celeste voiced by Saori Onishi (Momoko Maeda in My Love Story with Yamada-kun at Lv999)

  • Alice Wonderland voiced by Kanon Takao (Luka in In the Land of Leadale)

 

Based on the series of isekai fantasy light novels written by Nazuna Miki and illustrated by Subachi, the My Unique Skill Makes Me OP even at Level 1 TV anime is directed by Takeyuki Yanase and features animation production by Maho Film. The series will stream on Crunchyroll, who describe the story as follows:

 

Sato Ryota, a salaryman working for an exploitative company, suddenly finds himself inside an unfamiliar dungeon in a strange world where monsters drop all sorts of items as loot. With the help of a girl he happens to run into named Emily, he's able to check his own stats... and finds that all of them, both physical and magical, are at rank F (the weakest)! What's more, his level is stuck at 1 (the lowest)! Ryota is on the verge of utter despair... but then he learns that he also has "Drop Skill: All S," the most powerful unique skill there is! Can Ryota manage to survive in this bizarre world?! The strongest and weakest adventure of all is about to begin!

data.content:
The compilation film isn't the only big event in the works for Aki Hamaji's BOCCHI THE ROCK! manga. There's also a stage play on the way, with performances planned for THEATER MILANO-Za in Tokyo from August 11 to August 20, 2023.

 

More details, including staff and cast, will be announced for LIVE STAGE BOCCHI THE ROCK! at a later date.

 

RELATED: BOCCHI THE ROCK! Anime Gets the Band Back Together for Compilation Film

The series aired from October to December 2022 on Japanese TV and streamed on Crunchyroll. Crunchyroll describes the series: 

 

Hitori Gotoh, “Bocchi-chan,” is a girl who’s so introverted and shy around people that she’d always start her conversations with “Ah...”

 

During her middle school years, she started playing the guitar, wanting to join a band because she thought it could be an opportunity for even someone shy like her to also shine. But because she had no friends, she ended up practicing guitar for six hours every day all by herself.

data.title: FEATURE: My Home Hero and the Courage of Fatherhood
data.author: A. Trejo Mosquera
data.description:
Let's review this family story on Father's Day

Who better to recognize on Father's Day than the humble salesman turned hero that leads the anime My Home Hero, Tetsuo Tosu? Tetsuo demonstrates the courage of simply being a father, the first hero many of us ever had.
data.content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers for Episode 11 of My Home Hero.

 

It is said that being a parent is the most difficult job in the world, and it makes sense, you are responsible for another life for the rest of yours. In the world of anime, we have many examples of wonderful parents and a similar number of terrible parents. There are also plenty of fathers who are absent from their children's stories — that is not the case with Tetsuo Tosu, the protagonist of the anime My Home Hero.

 

The anime adaptation of Naoki Yamakawa's suspense manga with illustrations by Masashi Asaki premiered on April 2, its run through the spring anime season culminates appropriately on Father's Day. What better time to honor the courage fatherhood requires than by talking about one of the bravest fathers anime and manga have to offer?
 

An Ordinary Man Capable of Everything
 

 

Tetsuo Tosu is an ordinary man. Unlike other anime fathers who have near-superhuman or out-of-this-world abilities, the protagonist of My Home Hero is seemingly the most normal of guys. However, he would go to any lengths to protect his family.

 

When we first meet him, it's in his almost pathetic attempt to reconnect with his college student daughter, Reika. As soon as he realizes that the young woman is being mistreated by her boyfriend, Tetsuo does not hesitate to take extreme measures to protect her safety, even at the cost of becoming a murderer.

 

Being a parent requires sacrifice, from waking up in the middle of the night to tend to your crying baby to breaking your back working to ensure their future. Tetsuo is the kind of father who does not only what is expected of him as a father but is also willing to go the extra mile and sacrifice his soul if necessary to ensure the safety of his family. 

 

Faced with the fact that his daughter will continue to be the target of a criminal organization even after the death of her abusive boyfriend, Tetsuo decides to cover up the crime with the help of his equally brave wife, Kasen. Together they must continue fighting to avoid detection and also destroy the criminals in the process. A task that seems very complicated for a simple salesman fond of mystery novels and a housewife, especially when they are up against ruthless and clever criminals.

 

Not All Fatherly Love is Healthy

 

 

Tetsuo is not the only example of fatherly love My Home Hero offers us. Yoshitatsu Matori, Nobuto's father, is an expert con man who works for the criminal syndicate at the center of the story. Like our protagonist, Yoshitatsu deeply loves his son, but he has not been the best example or guide for the young man.

 

Yoshitatsu suffers from the very beginning, not knowing for sure if his son where his son is. When in the penultimate episode of the anime this other father decides to investigate the crime scene for himself, he cannot help but crumble under the realization that he has lost his son for good. Witnessing another father's suffering, Tetsuo offers to turn himself in to the authorities. But seeing Yoshitatsu will not be satisfied with that, and that his wife and daughter are in danger, once again the protagonist of the story decides to fight to protect them.

 

While it is difficult to empathize with Yoshitatsu's methods and his role as Nobuto's father, it is clear that his love for his son is sincere and that he is willing to do anything for him. In a certain way, Tetsuo and Yoshitatsu are a reflection of the other and two examples of paternal love expressed in two different ways: One seeking to protect, the other to avenge.

 

My Home Hero’s anime concludes today, though manga readers know that there is more to come and everything gets even more complicated. Tetsuo, Kasen and Reika will have to go past their limits to save their family and the story will show us other examples of parents, although none more dedicated than the humble salesman who leads this show. Tetsuo Tosu is an ordinary father, like any other, but facing extraordinary circumstances, he becomes a hero. Today I can only wish all anime-loving parents have a great day, you are our heroes too.

 

What other ordinary anime parents are heroes for you? Let me know in the comments below!
 

 

Watch My Home Hero on Crunchyroll

 

 

 

Amílcar Trejo Mosquera is a writer for Crunchyroll News. He also writes for O'kuroku Webzine (in spanish, sorry) and you can find him on Twitch, Twitter or Instagram.
